entities.name: Phenylephrine
observations: In a randomized within-infant study of 30 premature infants, one 5% phenylephrine drop plus two 0.5% tropicamide drops increased normalized pupil surface area to 43.8% ± 7.3%, versus 23.1% ± 8.3% with tropicamide alone (ratio 1.90; p<0.0001).
The same combination increased normalized pupil diameter to 65.9% ± 8.8%, versus 47.3% ± 8.7% with tropicamide alone (approximately 1.39-fold; p<0.0001).

entities.name: Tropicamide
observations: In the direct neonatal comparison, three drops of 0.5% tropicamide alone produced normalized pupil surface area of 23.1% ± 8.3% and normalized pupil diameter of 47.3% ± 8.7%.
Retinal periphery visualization was possible in 16/30 eyes (53.3%) with tropicamide alone versus 30/30 eyes (100%) with phenylephrine plus tropicamide; p<0.0001.

entities.name: Retinopathy of prematurity
observations: The evidence concerns premature infants undergoing retinal screening for retinopathy of prematurity; the accessible record did not provide detailed gestational age, postnatal age, or birth-weight distributions.

entities.name: PMID:27519933
observations: A prospective randomized double-blind within-infant study compared one eye receiving three 0.5% tropicamide drops with the fellow eye receiving one 5% phenylephrine plus two 0.5% tropicamide drops in 30 premature infants.
The combination was approximately twice as effective for normalized pupil surface area, but not for linear pupil diameter; retinal periphery visualization was 100% versus 53.3%.
Evidence is limited by the small sample, single direct study, fellow-eye design, and unavailable detailed safety and neonatal subgroup data.
